correctness.rationale: For the 12-edge simple cube, maximality requires the unmatched vertices to be independent, not that the matching be perfect. The independently written exhaustive check recovered 9 perfect and 8 nonperfect maximal matchings and checked all 4096 support traces. It recovered exactly the disjoint supports of size at most three other than co-directional triples, with f-polynomial 1+12z+42z²+32z³ and facet orbits 6, 24, 8. Each first positive branch has 5 hypotheses, fewer than the 8 a depth-four tree requires on that branch; any shattered triple gives depth three. The one-skeleton is connected: for any two cube edges there is an edge disjoint from both, since at most ten of the twelve edges can meet their endpoints. The signed degree-two boundary has exact rank 25 and the specified minor has determinant +1; the image is primitive, so H₁ has no torsion and rank 42−11−25=6, and the free H₂ has rank 32−25=7. The finite certificate exhausts this cube only and asserts no homotopy decomposition.
residual_risks: The rank and integral primitivity are verified for this finite matrix only; they provide no extension to larger cubes.

value.rationale: The natural smallest three-dimensional cube gives a complete test of whether feasible matching supports also realize every deletion pattern. The single geometric obstruction among three-matchings and the six stranded pair facets explain failure of purity; the simultaneous free H₁ and H₂ distinguish the trace complex from the ordinary matching complex. These exact facts can serve as a baseline for larger cube edge-query systems rather than merely counting known matchings.
